slides.0.title: Idaho, Virginia and Texas at a glance
slides.0.subtitle: Three smaller wine states
slides.1.title: Idaho: the Snake River Valley
slides.1.highlights.0.title: 9 April 2007
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Idaho's first AVA; about 5.29 million acres, with about 1,800 planted across 46 vineyards at approval; covers Idaho and Oregon (Malheur and Baker counties)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Climate
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Semi-arid desert; 10–12 inches of rain, so irrigation is needed; roughly 2,165–3,412 feet; about 1,475–1,515 growing degree days
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Grapes and sub-AVA
slides.1.highlights.2.content: 23 varieties including Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Chardonnay and Pinot Noir; the sub-AVA is Eagle Foothills
slides.1.content: The Snake River Valley spans Idaho and Oregon: another cross-state AVA.
slides.2.title: Virginia: Monticello
slides.2.highlights.0.title: History
slides.2.highlights.0.content: In the 1770s Jefferson backed Filippo Mazzei, who planted vines in 1774; Norton became available in 1830 and a Norton-based wine from the Monticello Wine Company won an award in Vienna in 1873; the Zonin family invested in Barboursville in 1976
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Monticello AVA
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Approved 23 January 1984 as Virginia's fourth appellation; expanded by about 106,000 acres in 2019; about 30 varieties, led by Cabernet Franc, Chardonnay and Viognier
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Climate
slides.2.highlights.2.content: East slope of the Blue Ridge; cold air drains through gaps, keeping it 4–5°F warmer than surroundings; about 39–44 inches of rain
slides.2.content: Virginia has one of America's longest wine stories, but humid summers remain a long-term challenge.
slides.3.title: Texas: the High Plains and Hill Country
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Texas High Plains
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Approved 2 March 1993; about 8 million acres with over 3,700 planted; mostly 3,000–4,000 feet; nearly half of the state's commercial wine grapes come from here
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Texas Hill Country
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Approved 1991; over 9 million acres, the second-largest AVA in the US, with fewer than 800 acres planted
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Grapes
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Tempranillo and Cabernet Sauvignon are the most planted; Texas has eight AVAs, and Bell Mountain (1986) was the first entirely in Texas
slides.3.content: Texas shows that an AVA's size is not its vineyard area.
